No rushing, no memory-trusting. Release protocol 10 gates WED → SUN Research to final lock “ We can't control the outcome. We control the data, the process, the structure — aligned for maximum points. — Garrett Baxley 01 Standard process 02 Lessons learned 03 Mans study 04 Our Core Four 05 Simulations 06 Input templates 07 Scorecard 01 / 07 The standard process Weekly cadence for the Sun–Mon slate. Every input has a time. Every decision passes the same gates. Wednesday Data pull from locked sources + full QB pool scan. Every starting QB is priced and tiered. No QB locks before the scan completes. Thursday Position pools, stack candidates, Jeff Mans Core Four study. Friday Garrett's calls logged. Dad's research added. Saturday Build lineups. Run all gates. Sunday AM Weather + inactives verification. Final lock. Ten-gate system Gates 00–09 · final lock follows GATE 00 Data lock Locked v1 sources: DraftKings salaries + ownership; FantasyGuru.com (Jeff Mans Core Four); Weather.com game-day readings (never narratives); official inactive reports; GSE engine signals. No swapping sources mid-week. GATE 01 QB pool scan Every starter priced/tiered; cheap QBs with rushing floors flagged as value. GATE 02 Game-pick firewall Team fades don't eliminate opposing players. GATE 03 Stack rules QB + max 2 same-team pass-catchers; no TE at FLEX; full $50,000 spent. GATE 04 Injury gate Any flag = player removed, no exceptions. GATE 05 Weather gate Numbers verified within hours of lock; narratives rejected. GATE 06 Garbage-time discount 4th-quarter trailing volume discounted hard. GATE 07 Thesis-to-roster audit Every written thesis has a rostered player. GATE 08 Garrett's calls Logged pre-lock, scored post-slate, never ignored. GATE 09 Simulations 10,000+ correlated slates before lock; lineups need top-decile ceiling and positive sim ROI vs field. Final: Lock All ten gates pass or the lineup doesn't ship. 02 / 07 Lessons learned This log records failures by both Motif and Garrett. Garrett's rule: if he missed, it goes in. No egos, just signal. [part 2] OUNDATION / 01 What it is One QB, one RB, one WR, one TE — the foundation a lineup is built around. Not the four highest-projected players: cost and value are co-equal inputs. One value piece frees up money for a stud elsewhere. Published Fridays on FantasyGuru.com in Mans' DFS NFL Cash Game Breakdown . The Friday panel show is separate and hosted by Tyler Buecher. METHOD / 02 His theory Objective: “Beat the optimizers.” The field runs the same vanilla projections through optimizers, so he builds cash-game lineups as the kryptonite of that — then funds GPPs with cash winnings. Cash preferences: dual-threat QBs with rushing floors (“dual-threat quarterbacks are our jam in cash games”); willing to pay up at TE when volume is elite, with no blanket never-pay-up rule; and ownership discipline. Chalky value is playable, but cap how many chalk pieces the build carries. A chalk fade is a legitimate differentiator. He runs separate cash and GPP Core Fours. PIPELINE / 03 His weekly pipeline 01 Weather: wind and total effects per game. 02 Vegas: team totals, spreads and over/unders; implied totals anchor game selection. 03 Price tiers: positional tiers on each site; the four can differ because pricing differs. 04 OL vs DL: the “Mans Model” grades each line from −100 to +100. 05 Coverage: which corners shadow which WRs. 06 Don't Forget About…: cheaper pivots with similar roles. 07 Favorite GPP Play…: per position, same game environment, lower ownership. 08 Sunday update: late news folded into the pool before lock. WEEKS / 01 + 03 Sept 10–14 + Sept 27, 2026 Picks not public His Week 1 and Week 3 picks are behind the FantasyGuru.com paywall. They are not listed here rather than guessed. Verified breadcrumbs only: his Week 1 build was hurt by Joe Burrow disappointing; his Week 2 cash Core Four QB was Caleb Williams, who got injured. If a FantasyGuru subscription is added, his Friday four get tracked here weekly against ours. TRANSFER / 04 What we steal The pipeline maps 1:1 onto our gates: weather gate, value logic, ownership discipline and the Sunday update. Our edge: the repo's exact optimizer plus payout simulation — tools his readers don't have. 04 / 07 Our Core Four Week Player Pos Salary Why Result Week 3 2026-09-27 — — — Set under the new process starting Week 4 — Week 3 was built under the old rushed process and is scored in the autopsy, not here. 05 / 07 Simulations Operating standard: 10,000+ correlated simulated slates per week before lock. 01 Correlated player distributions: QB-WR stacks, DST matchups. 02 Simulated field for cash-line estimation. 03 Leverage and exposure analysis. Runs on the repo's own tools — payout-sim.ts (portfolio ROI vs simulated field) and the correlation GPP layer — once the live slate provider is registered. No separate engine needed; the repo already had it. 06 / 07 Input templates Read-only formats for weekly additions. Copy the field structure when sending research or calls. [part 1] GSE DFS Process System DraftKings NFL · Weekly Operations GSE DFS Process System The repeatable weekly machine for DraftKings NFL DFS. Same data, same gates, every week. No rushing, no memory-trusting. “We can't control the outcome. We control the data, the process, the structure — aligned for maximum points.” — Garrett Baxley 01 Process 02 Lessons 03 Mans Study 04 Core Four 05 Simulations 06 Inputs 07 Scorecard SECTION 01 The Standard Process 0 / 10 operational gates clear this session Weekly cadence for the Sun–Mon slate. Lock the source baseline, then clear all ten numbered gates. Every gate is a hard stop: it must pass before the process moves forward. Wednesday Data pull from the locked source set + full QB pool scan (every starting QB on the slate, priced and tiered — no QB is locked before the scan is complete). Thursday Position pools, stack candidates, Jeff Mans Core Four study. Friday Garrett's calls logged in the input zone; Dad's research added. Saturday Build lineups; run every gate and audit below. Sunday AM Weather + inactives verification; final lock. BASE Data Lock Same sources every week. Locked v1 set: DraftKings salaries + ownership; Fantasy Alarm (Jeff Mans Core Four + show notes); weather verification (Weather.com game-day reading, not narratives); official inactive reports; GSE engine signals from Garrett's database. No swapping projection sources mid-week. 01 QB Pool Scan Every starting QB priced and tiered before any lineup is built. Cheap QBs with rushing floors and home games get flagged as value, never skipped. 02 Game-Pick Firewall Team fades do not eliminate opposing players. The QB of a team you pick against can still be the slate's best value. 03 Stack Rules QB + max 2 same-team pass-catchers. No TE at FLEX. Full $50,000 salary spent. 04 Injury Gate Any injury flag = player removed from the pool. No exceptions, no “he'll play through it.” 05 Weather Gate Every weather claim verified with a number from the locked source within hours of lock. Narratives without numbers are rejected. 06 Garbage-Time Discount Fourth-quarter trailing production is discounted hard in evaluation. Chasing volume is not a role change. 07 Thesis-to-Roster Audit Every written game thesis must have a rostered player. If you write “Detroit blows out the Jets,” a Lion is in the lineup. 08 Garrett's Calls His picks are logged pre-lock in the input zone and scored post-slate. Never ignored, never changed just because he said so — verified against results. 09 Simulations Thousands of Monte Carlo slate simulations before lock ( 10,000+ ). Lineups must show top-decile ceiling and positive sim ROI vs the simulated field. No lineup ships on vibes; it ships on sims. 10 Lock Checklist All gates above pass, salary fully spent, no flagged injuries, weather verified, sims run. If a gate fails, the lineup does not ship. 10 pull-ups. 92/100 efficiency. About 9 kcal. Every joint tracked by AI 🤖

I filmed one set on the doorway bar and ran it through a 33-point body-pose model, with a second, independent tracker double-checking the count (both say 10). Every rep got graded on range of motion, control on the way down, lock-out at the bottom, hip sway, pull speed and left/right symmetry — and, with my height and weight (188 cm, 79 kg), a rough energy cost and an effort score.

What the numbers said:
✅ 8 clean chin-at-bar reps, 10 of 10 full hangs at the bottom, ~4 cm of body sway — strict⚡ ~414 J of work per rep, 350 W best pull, peak ~850 W 📉 pull speed dropped 46 % from rep 3 to rep 10 — rep 10 took 1.7× the effort of rep 3 for the same work🔥 ~0.9 kcal per rep, ~9 kcal for the set (rough model, not a measurement)↔️ my left elbow reads ~16° more bent than my right at the top on every rep — some of that is the camera angle, some might be me.

The model also caught that I stand holding the bar for 5 s before my feet leave the floor — the arms lengthen 9 % and the shoulders sink 6 cm the moment the weight goes on.

The heat map on my body is not a thermal camera: it's where surface-EMG studies say a pull-up works (lats ~124 % MVIC, biceps 78, infraspinatus 75, traps 52, pecs 44, obliques 33 — Youdas et al. 2010, J Strength Cond Res; concentric > eccentric from Dickie et al. 2017, J Electromyogr Kinesiol), warmed up by how hard each of my reps actually was — and the whole body warms through the set with my measured speed loss, because velocity loss tracks metabolic fatigue and doesn't recover between reps (Sánchez-Medina & González-Badillo 2011, Med Sci Sports Exerc).
